subject: Private deployment: cost model & next steps for environment licensing
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap + ask: private/VPC pricing and unit economics

Sanjay — thanks again for the call this morning. Short recap and a few asks so we can put together a formal quote: 

- Scope: private/VPC deployment for Acme’s customer-facing chat assistant (production) and a staging environment. You mentioned intent to move first 2 product lines in H1.
- Key unknowns we need to price: typical monthly token volumes (min/typical/peak), target budget range for the program, and number of private environments you want (prod + staging + sandbox?).

To move quickly on pricing we need 3 numbers from your side: 
1) Estimated monthly token volume (low / expected / peak). Example format: 5M / 20M / 50M tokens.
2) Target spend range (monthly) you have in mind for the first 6–12 months.
3) Number of private environments (e.g., 1 prod, 1 staging, 2 dev sandboxes) and whether the staging environment requires identical capacity SLA.

A note on licensing models we’ll include in the quote (we can tailor): 
- Committed token pool + overage: straightforward for heavy usage; discounts at larger commits.
- Environment-based license: one-time or annual environment fee + per-token usage; preferred when teams want fixed environment isolation.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs): fixed monthly fee by capacity, useful when predictable latency and throughput are required.

If you can reply with the 3 items above, I’ll loop in Ben with a few modeled scenarios (target $/1M token bands, seat/env fees, and support tiers) and return a formal quote + draft mutual action plan.

Thanks — next step is a procurement/price call if you and Procurement want that.

Best,
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0132

From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@acme.com>

Date: 2026-10-12T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + ask: private/VPC pricing and unit economics

Thanks Irene — appreciate the clear notes. Answers below: 

1) Token volumes (monthly): low 10M / expected 30M / peak 75M. These are across both product lines combined; split roughly 70/30 prod:staging.
2) Budget range: for initial rollout we have a target monthly run-rate of $25k–$40k, with potential to expand if performance and cost targets are met. FY27 budget could open to $80k+/mo depending on pilot outcomes.
3) Environments: we need 1 prod (SLA), 1 staging (near-prod), and 1 dev sandbox. Staging should be able to handle up to 50% of prod capacity during rehearsals.

Questions from our side: 
- How do you typically handle pricing for fully air-gapped on-prem installs? Is there an additional license uplift?
- What are the support tiers and related SLAs — which tier would you recommend for our usage?
- Do you have a SOC2 package / summary we can forward to security?

Procurement (cc’d) will coordinate any PO-level questions. We want a short timeline: aim to have a draft quote by end of next week if possible.

—Sanjay
Head of Product, Acme Corp
Sanjay.Patel@acme.com

Subject: Re: Quick recap + ask: private/VPC pricing and unit economics — initial scenarios

Sanjay — following up with three high-level scenarios based on the ranges you provided. Attaching a short pricing model PDF (redwood_private_pricing_model_v1.pdf) and SOC2 summary.

Scenario A — Committed token pool (recommended for predictable unit economics):
- Commit: 30M tokens/mo
- List band: $1,800 / 1M tokens at this commit level (effective $54k/mo).
- Overage: $2,500 / 1M tokens above commit.
- Environments: prod + staging included; additional dev sandbox $1,500/mo environment fee.
- Support: Standard (business hours, 24hr incident response for Sev 1).

Scenario B — Environment-license + usage (good for strict isolation):
- Annual environment license: $45k/year for prod environment (includes reserved control plane capacity), $20k/year for staging.
- Usage: $3,200 / 1M tokens (metered).
- Dev sandbox: $6k/year.
- Support: Enterprise tier recommended for SLA parity with annual license (24/7+SLA credits).

Scenario C — Dedicated GPU capacity (SLA + lowest per-token cost at scale):
- Fixed monthly capacity fee (varies by GPU type); example: $28k/mo for capacity to handle expected prod throughput, includes stage at 50% load.
- Effective token economics after batching/caching: $1,200–$1,600 / 1M tokens (depending on model and caching).
- Support: Enterprise (24/7, dedicated TAM, escalation path).

Rough examples against your expected 30M tokens: 
- Scenario A: ~$54k/mo (committed price)
- Scenario B: ~$96k/yr env license amortized + metered usage (~$96k+ depending on usage)
- Scenario C: ~$36k–$48k/mo effective (capacity fee + marginal token costs) but gives best latency and cost at scale.

Notes and tradeoffs:
- We can provide hybrid pricing (env license + committed token pool) which is common for on-prem customers.
- Air-gapped/on-prem installs typically have a one-time deployment fee and slightly higher annual maintenance (we’ll capture that in the quote).
- Support tier recommendation: Enterprise for prod-critical workloads (TAM + 24/7). Enterprise adds ~15–25% uplift to fees depending on chosen model.

See attached for an exported model with line items and example PO text. Will include a short mutual action plan spreadsheet for sign-off.

Best,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_private_pricing_model_v1.pdf (pricing scenarios), SOC2_summary.pdf (compliance snapshot)
